Mount it, assign an experiment to each tube, and let the system work through the queue on its own, whether that's after hours or during a busy day at the bench.

faqs.question: What is the AUTOsample-60 used for?
faqs.answer: The AUTOsample-60 is a top-mounting autosampler for the Nanalysis-60 benchtop NMR spectrometer. It automates sample runs across two 25-tube carousels, enabling unattended, walk-away operation.

faqs.question: How many samples can the AUTOsample-60 run at once?
faqs.answer: The AUTOsample-60 holds 50 tubes across two carousels of 25 tubes each. Onboard queueing software runs through the full set automatically.

faqs.question: Does the AUTOsample-60 need extra bench space?
faqs.answer: No, the AUTOsample-60 mounts on top of the Nanalysis-60 and doesn't require any additional bench space.

faqs.question: Can I switch between automated and manual sampling?
faqs.answer: Yes, the AUTOsample-60 allows quick interconversion between autosampler and manual modes as needed.

faqs.question: Can the AUTOsample-60 run multiple experiments per sample?
faqs.answer: Yes, the onboard queueing software can assign a full sequence per tube, supporting structural elucidation routines like 1H, COSY, HMBC, HSQC, and DEPT-135.

faqs.question: Does the AUTOsample-60 save data automatically?
faqs.answer: Yes, data is acquired and saved automatically as each queued experiment completes.

faqs.question: Which instrument is the AUTOsample-60 compatible with?
faqs.answer: The AUTOsample-60 is compatible with the Nanalysis-60 benchtop NMR spectrometer.

faqs.question: Can the AUTOsample-60 run overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, the onboard queueing software is built for unattended operation, letting a full batch run overnight or after work hours.

faqs.question: What is the price of the AUTOsample-60 in India?
faqs.answer: The price of the AUTOsample-60 in India depends on your configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Nanalysis AUTOsample-60 in India. Inkarp provides demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

body.text: It mounts on top of the Nanalysis-60 and switches quickly between autosampler and manual modes, without needing any extra bench space.
Two carousels, each holding 25 tubes, give it a 50-tube capacity across a single setup.
Onboard queueing software lets you assign an experiment to each tube individually, then run the whole set automatically without staying at the bench.
It's built to maximize efficiency by improving throughput during work hours or after them, letting a queue run overnight or during a lunch break.
Beyond simple 1D runs, it can handle a full series of experiments per sample, supporting basic structural elucidation routines like 1H, COSY, HMBC, HSQC, and DEPT-135.
Data is acquired and saved automatically as the queue runs, so results are ready and organized by the time you're back at the instrument.

sections.title: Unattended Queueing and Throughput
sections.tabSummary: How the onboard software runs a queue automatically
body: Getting more out of an instrument usually means running it when nobody's watching, and that's exactly the gap AUTOsample-60 closes.

Setup starts with assigning an experiment to each tube through the onboard queueing software. Once that's done, the carousels take over, running through all 50 tubes in sequence without needing anyone at the bench. That means a queue can run overnight, over a lunch break, or in the background of a busy day, improving throughput without adding staff time. Data is acquired and saved automatically as each experiment finishes, so results are organized and waiting by the time you check back in.

groups.title: Structural Elucidation Routines
groups.description: A single 1D spectrum doesn't always tell the full story. AUTOsample-60 is built to run the fuller picture automatically, one sample at a time.
body: Rather than limiting each tube to a single experiment, the queueing software can assign a full sequence per sample, covering routines like 1H, COSY, HMBC, HSQC, and DEPT-135. That turns basic structural elucidation into something that runs unattended across an entire carousel, rather than requiring a researcher to set up and monitor each step by hand.
